title: prefill/decode: chunked speculative prefill + stage-overlap KV scheduler optimizations
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Prefill (KV cache population) and decode phases are a major source of wasted GPU cycles for long-context workloads. We observed head-of-line stalls when large prefill batches serialized kernel work and memory copies; large contiguous prefill allocations also increased peak memory and reduced effective batching for concurrent requests. This PR implements three coordinated improvements: 1) chunked prefill to split large prefill sequences into configurable micro-batches so memory spikes are bounded and other work can interleave; 2) speculative prefill: when decode enters steady-state we asynchronously start a speculative prefill for likely next-chunk keys (heuristic+LRU hinting) to reduce decode stalls; 3) a stage-overlap-aware KV scheduler and kernel dispatch path that prefers non-blocking kernel launches and opportunistic execution of lightweight KV operations while heavy decode kernels are running. Changes also include KV cache compaction, improved lock-free queueing for continuous batching, and unit/integration + perf tests. Summary of benefits (internal perf bench): end-to-end throughput +14-18% for multi-turn long-context (16k+ tokens) with 15% reduction in P95 latency; tail memory usage down ~22% on A100 runs and sustained throughput improved when concurrency > 8. Backwards-compatible: conservatively enabled behind feature flag `prefill_chunked_speculative_v2` with default on for release builds after initial canary.

review_comments: Diego Morales: Nice end-to-end improvements. Two questions: (1) the speculative prefill heuristic - can you explain how false positives are bounded and whether we ever evict speculative keys prematurely? (2) any safety implications if speculative prefill fails mid-decode?

Aisha Patel: Answered: speculative prefill uses a weighted hint combining recent-token n-grams and LRU hot keys. We bound memory by a per-request speculative quota and compaction will drop speculative entries first. If speculative prefill fails or is evicted, decode falls back to normal prefill synchronously; correctness unchanged, only latency impacted.

Priya Singh: Tests look good, but please add an integration test that runs with small GPU memory to validate compaction behavior. Also please add a flag to disable speculative prefill at runtime for canarying.
Aisha Patel: Added test_kv_compactor and feature flag `prefill_chunked_speculative_v2` that can be toggled at runtime. Updated bench scripts to run with OOM-sized toy traces.
Liam O'Connor: Kernel dispatch changes are subtle - did you validate with mixed model topologies? Any perf regressions on short-context workloads?

Aisha Patel: We ran the dispatcher against 7 model families (gpt-style, multi-head, transformer-xl variants). Short-context (<512) showed <1% variance; long-context improved as reported. Added safeguard: scheduler falls back to prior path if a specific kernel combination is unsupported on a target GPU.
Diego Morales: Approved after minor doc fixes.
